Read-only task in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Change NO files. Do not commit or push. Do NOT write any .md report file — return findings as your final text message only.

TASK: Mine GitHub PR #59 (ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa, "SFCC-55 global footer UI") for every CodeRabbit review finding that was DECLINED / not fixed, plus the reasoning given in the human reply.

Commands to use (run them, they may produce large output — page through with head/sed/grep rather than dumping everything):
- `gh pr view 59 --comments` (full)
- `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/59/comments --paginate` (inline review comments — this is where CodeRabbit's line-level findings and the in-thread replies live)
- `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/59/reviews --paginate`
- `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/issues/59/comments --paginate`

Tip: use `--jq` to project only `{id, in_reply_to_id, user: .user.login, path, line, body}` so output stays manageable, then read individual bodies as needed.

WHAT I NEED BACK, structured:

1. **DECLINED findings** — for each one:
   - The file path / line CodeRabbit flagged
   - A 1-2 sentence summary of what CodeRabbit claimed
   - The verbatim (or near-verbatim, quoted) key reasoning from the reply explaining WHY it was not fixed
   - **The transferable RULE this establishes** — i.e. what a future developer on this repo should now know. This is the most important part. E.g. "CodeRabbit flagged X; declined because this repo's .claude/rules/Y.md mandates Z — rule: always do Z here even though it looks like X."

2. **ACCEPTED findings that changed a convention** — any finding that was fixed AND where the fix established/clarified a project-wide pattern (not just a typo fix). Same format: finding → what changed → rule established.

3. **Anything the conversation flagged as DELIBERATELY DEFERRED / known compromise / "not fixing now"** — including from the PR body, human comments, or CodeRabbit thread replies. Note who deferred it and the stated reason.

4. Any place the conversation shows the footer code CONTRADICTING or working around a rule in .claude/rules/ or AGENTS.md (e.g. a Tier 1 file touched, a rule doc that had to be corrected because the code diverged, an exception granted).

Be exhaustive on the declines — that's the core ask. Quote real text. If a thread is ambiguous about whether it was fixed or declined, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

TITLE: feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI — shell, layout, and ui-kit component structure
STATE: MERGED | base: develop | head: feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui
---BODY---
# Description

Builds the global footer per SFCC-55 — shell, layout, and component structure across
all eight storefronts and both breakpoints. Content is Contentful-shaped but
fixture-backed: the CMS integration, link destinations, and Omneo sign-up are
separate stories, so `FooterContainer` supplies `FOOTER_FIXTURE` and `Footer` itself
takes its content as a required prop and fetches nothing.

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are
  in the history; the parts worth keeping were adopted deliberately as separate
  commits (`fix(button)`, `feat(footer)`, `test(ui-kit)`) rather than folded into
  conflict resolution, so what came from upstream and why stays visible.
- **9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `pre-commit` hook
  regenerates it on any `components/`/`hooks/`/`utils/` change and `git add`s it.
  Mechanical — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx` carries a pre-existing `fontSize="l"` (invalid token) and a
`useCurrentBasket` call from the original copy-first import. Both predate this PR —
our diff there is comments only — but they surface in the changed-files view.

# Linked

- Ticket: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI). Design: Figma *Zimmermann_Design_System_2026*;
  footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 3

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad B

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `components/footer/` — footer assembly, subscribe section + modal, contact icon row,
  bottom bar; Contentful-shaped fixture and schema placeholder
- `theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`,
  not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name
  inherits it rather than replacing it
- `components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of
  the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted
- `theme/fontFace.tsx` + `static/fonts/` — self-hosted Futura Round, mounted in both the
  app and Storybook from one module so the two cannot drift
- `components/icons/` — the four Zimmermann chevrons, replacing base-template
  substitutions that rendered a filled glyph where the design is a 1px stroke
- `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` — colour derivation moved out of the hook into the
  recipe, so the recipe is the single styling surface
- `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — prop extraction scoped to `<ComponentName>Props`,
  Markdown table cells escaped, comma-containing types no longer silently dropped

# How to test-drive this PR

- `npm run env -- dev && npm start` → `/`, scroll to the footer. Nav columns hug their
  content with even gaps; hovering a link underlines it
- Resize through **1030px → 760px** — the bottom bar stays aligned with the content above
  it at every width
- Type a valid email → `>` opens the Join Us modal; empty or malformed is blocked inline
  with no modal
- `npm run storybook` → `Layout/Footer` (4 states incl. modal-open), `Elements/ZimmNavItem`
  (unsafe-href fallback), `Forms/ZimmInputAction` (validation)

# Protection-tier check

> ⚠️ **Tier 1** — `.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}` (test config, **Integration-owned**)
> for serving and mounting the self-hosted fonts; `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`
> (governance, **both squad leads + Integration lead**) to record them;
> `theme/foundation/sizes.ts` (design system, **UI-Designer-owned**) — whitespace only,
> and it now diffs to **zero** against `develop`.
> Authenticated as `marcelannavarro`, a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `components/footer/`, `components/header/` (comments only),
> `theme/components/` (**UI-Designer — notified**). `components/footer/` is Global Shell,
> owned by **both squads** — Squad A notified.

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (3 pre-existing `header` unused-import warnings, documented in-file)
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 168/168
- [x] Storybook interaction — 15 `play` functions across 7 stories
- [x] Runtime behaviour — 20/20 (hover, focus-visible, validation, modal focus trap + Escape + focus restore, overlay z-index above the sticky header)

# PR #59 (SFCC-55 global footer UI) — CodeRabbit findings mined

**PR state:** MERGED · `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` → `develop` · 58 actionable comments across 9 review rounds · 57 inline threads.

Two threads were fixed with **no in-thread reply at all** (auto-marked "Addressed in commits"): `.claude/registry/hooks.md:62` and `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:94`. That technically breaks AGENTS.md's "always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding" rule.

---

## 1. DECLINED FINDINGS

### 1A. Declined as invalid / not-applicable (CodeRabbit withdrew)

---

**D1 — `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` (L27-36) — "Obtain Tier 1 approval before merging"**

Claim: file is Tier 1 Governance; needs an approving code-owner review from `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before it can be edited.

Reply: *"Not changing this, and recording why so the same pattern isn't re-flagged... AGENTS.md's 'Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced' section provides a verified-session exception: the authenticated `gh` identity is checked against `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, and if it is a member the edit may proceed after naming the file and the reason. That check was run — `marcelannavarro` is a member — and both the file and the reason are named in the commit bodies of `af87b5b` and `f8d2f75`... Note the real merge gate is unaffected either way — CODEOWNERS routes this path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` and branch protection requires that review before merge, independently of this workflow step."*

> **RULE:** A Tier 1 file *may* be edited in-session by a verified `tier-1-approvers` member, provided the commit body names the file and the reason. Claude's pause-to-ask is a workflow step, not the gate — CODEOWNERS + branch protection is. State the `gh api user` check explicitly in the reply so it's auditable.

---

**D2 — `.storybook/main.js` + `.storybook/preview.tsx` — "Revert the protected Storybook configuration" (raised TWICE, threads 2 and 20)**

Claim: guidelines say `.storybook/**` must never be modified; remove `staticDirs` and the `ZimmFontFace` decorator.

**A3 — `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts` — the unsafe-href guard (threads 5 + 15)**

Original finding: unguarded Contentful URLs reaching `href`. Fixed by extracting `isSafeHref` to a shared util used by both the footer and `ZimmNavItem`; a rejected/absent value falls through to *"a labelled non-interactive `<span>`, which is the correct treatment for 'no usable destination' and avoids a WCAG 2.4.4/3.2.4 false affordance."*

Then a second, deeper finding: *"three forms resolved off-site, not one"*. The fix: *"The lookahead is now `(?![/\\])`... The WHATWG URL parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from *anywhere* in the input, **before** it parses — so `/<TAB>/evil.com` is parsed as `//evil.com`. The guard was testing the raw string while the browser resolved a normalised one. It now normalises the same way the parser does and tests the result. **A plain space is deliberately left alone**, because the parser percent-encodes rather than removes it."*

The self-criticism is the transferable bit: *"all 13 cases were derived from the same mental model as the regex, and not one contained a backslash or a control character.
